chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu al-Ward, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the woman who is in the Dhuhr prayer and has already prayed two cycles, then she sees the blood. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She should rise from her place of prayer and not make up the two cycles. And if she saw the blood while she was in the Maghrib prayer and had already prayed two cycles, let her rise from her place of prayer. Then, when she is clean, let her make up the one cycle that was missed from Maghrib.'
ai.seo_question: What should a woman do with her prayer if she starts menstruating while performing it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'breaking' (iqtiḍāʾ) versus 'completing' (tamām) prayer when menstruation interrupts an obligatory act, distinguishing between prayers with fixed cycle counts. Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes that for Dhuhr, the two completed cycles are considered valid and final, whereas for Maghrib, the single remaining cycle is deferred until purification, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the integrity of the prayer unit relative to the impurity event. This ruling underscores the practical application of ritual purity (ṭahārah) as a condition for the validity of the remaining portion of the prayer.
